required_evidence: Construct the unique global nearest point for every x and prove the whole intersection is nonempty under the exact uniform finite-feasibility hypothesis.
Prove norm convergence of the full finite-subset net, with no assumption of a countable cofinal constraint family.
Determine the global optimal value exactly from the finite optimal values and prove the stated nonexpansive estimate.
critical_errors: Infer nonempty total intersection from finite feasibility alone while omitting the supplied uniform bound or an applicable compactness argument.
Replace the arbitrary finite-subset net by an unsupported enumeration or by an arbitrary sequence of finite subsets.
Claim only weak convergence, omit the global value identity, or assert linearity of a projection onto arbitrary convex sets.
Treat the global point, common intersection, or convergence as a supplied certificate.
completion_policy: Complete the whole constructive target. Any valid weak-compactness or direct Cauchy argument is accepted. The reference energy-error estimate is optional; proof length and the author route are not criteria.
open_task_policy: Accept every independently verified proof, counterexample and alternative construction satisfying the actual task. Explicit conditional results remain separate contributions. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof. No hidden proof-route, length or vocabulary requirements.
